$comment: Baseline verdict recorded by the original Node engine on a real government portal, before the pure-core extraction. The captures beside this file are that page with its identity removed — URLs, titles, selectors, text content and custom properties all replaced. None of that feeds the maths, which is why the verdict is unchanged; that it is unchanged is itself evidence the scrub touched nothing load-bearing. NOTE on the one deliberate re-baseline: earned moved 55.81 -> 55.80 when judged ratios began being computed FROM their counts (31/38 = 0.815789) instead of the rounded value restated beside them (0.816). Nothing measured changed. NOTE on A3: this capture predates the :focus-visible seeding fix, so its '80 of 80' finding is a known false positive of the old probe. It is pinned deliberately — captures without a `seeded` flag keep their original treatment, which is what makes this fixture a stable test of the scoring maths rather than of the probe. NOTE on the second deliberate re-baseline: 64.89 -> 65.20 when R2 (CSS logical properties) and M2 (prefers-reduced-motion) moved OUT of the 100 into the `extended` block, because DGA publishes neither and Figma cannot express either. Nothing measured changed and no finding changed — the two checks simply stopped counting toward a compliance score they had no authority behind. The arithmetic reconciles exactly: earned 55.80 - 0.99 (R2) - 2.00 (M2) = 52.81, available 86 - 3 - 2 = 81, and 52.82/81 = 65.20.
